title: Soil Management
text: Sustainable soil management supports soil functions including water regulation, nutrient cycling, carbon storage and biological activity. Management practices should be adapted to local soil and environmental conditions.

title: Soil Organic Carbon
text: Soil organic carbon is an important component of soil health. Maintaining and increasing soil organic carbon can support soil structure, nutrient cycling, water-related functions and soil biological activity.

title: State of the World's Land and Water Resources
text: Land and water resources are under pressure from climate change, land degradation and increasing demands. Sustainable management requires integrated approaches that consider soil, water, vegetation and human land use.

title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
text: Biodiversity and ecosystem services are affected by changes in land and sea use, direct exploitation, climate change, pollution and invasive alien species. Habitat loss and degradation can reduce biodiversity and ecosystem functions.

title: Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability
text: Climate change affects ecosystems through changes in temperature, precipitation, extreme events and other environmental conditions. Risks depend on exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity.

title: Convention on Biological Diversity
text: The Convention on Biological Diversity promotes conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components and fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources. Conservation and sustainable use are linked to ecosystem health.

title: Agroforestry
text: Agroforestry integrates trees with crops and/or livestock. It can provide habitat, diversify production and contribute to soil and ecosystem functions when appropriately designed for local conditions.

title: Conservation Agriculture
text: Conservation agriculture is based on principles including minimum soil disturbance, permanent soil cover and crop diversification. These practices can support soil health and improve resource-use efficiency when adapted to local conditions.

title: Assessment Report on Pollinators
text: Pollinators contribute to ecosystem functioning and food production. Pollinator abundance and diversity can be influenced by land-use change, agricultural practices, pesticides, habitat availability and climate conditions.

title: Ecosystem Restoration for People, Nature and Climate
text: Ecosystem restoration can support biodiversity, ecosystem services and human well-being. Restoration approaches should be appropriate to local ecological and social conditions.

title: Global Forest Resources Assessment
text: Forests provide habitat, regulate water and climate processes, store carbon and support livelihoods. Forest loss and degradation can affect biodiversity and ecosystem services.

title: Habitat Fragmentation
text: Habitat conversion and fragmentation can alter ecological connectivity and reduce the quality and availability of habitats for species. Maintaining and restoring habitat connectivity can support biodiversity.

title: Crop Diversification
text: Crop diversification can contribute to resilient agricultural systems. Combining or rotating crops can influence soil biological processes, resource use and habitat conditions.

title: Soil Moisture and Water Availability
text: Water availability is an important constraint for agricultural and ecosystem processes. Soil moisture depends on rainfall, soil properties, vegetation, land management and climatic conditions.

title: Environmental Pollution and Biodiversity
text: Pollution is one of the major direct drivers of biodiversity change. The effects depend on the pollutant, concentration, exposure pathway, ecosystem and species affected.

title: Climate Resilience and Ecosystems
text: Ecosystem resilience can be affected by climate hazards and other pressures. Reducing additional stresses and protecting ecosystem diversity can contribute to adaptive capacity.

title: Biodiversity Monitoring
text: Biodiversity monitoring supports assessment of changes in species, habitats and ecosystem conditions. Repeated observations and appropriate indicators can help identify trends and inform conservation decisions.
